Good day everyone,

I am writing an R function that uses a fitted secr model as an argument, and extracts various elements of the fitted model on the fly. A summary of an example model "obj" appears below.

Beta parameters (coefficients)
           beta    SE.beta       lcl       ucl
D     -5.055756 0.03377637 -5.121956 -4.989555
g0    -5.065061 0.16792064 -5.394180 -4.735943

Variance-covariance matrix of beta parameters
                 D           g0        sigma
D      0.001140843  0.000852937 -0.002759848
g0     0.000852937  0.028197342 -0.029797696
sigma -0.002759848 -0.029797696  0.049553587

Fitted (real) parameters evaluated at base levels of covariates
      link     estimate  SE.estimate          lcl          ucl
D      log 6.372549e-03 2.153030e-04 5.964344e-03 6.808692e-03
g0     log 6.313523e-03 1.067688e-03 4.542945e-03 8.774170e-03
sigma  log 2.825669e+03 6.368854e+02 1.826579e+03 4.371235e+03

I'm having trouble extracting the SE for density.  I can calculate the SE for density on the link scale from a full-likelihood model using:

sqrt(diag(solve(obj$fit$hessian)))[1]
[1] 0.03377637     # this matches SE.beta for D above

but clearly transforming this to the real scale isn't as simple as it is with the parameter estimates themselves.
exp(-5.055756) yields 0.006372547, the density estimate on the real scale (this also works for the confidence limits), but
exp(0.03377637) yields 1.034353, which is clearly not the SE on the real scale.

Can anyone help me understand how to calculate (or simply extract) the SE on the real scale from a fitted secr model object?

Thanks in advance,
Eric

How the different detection function influence the parameter estimates?

Thank you,
Ree

messages.subject: Re: parameters estimates from non- Half-normal detection function
messages.subject_clean: parameters estimates from non- Half-normal detection function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ree
The interpretation of the parameters labelled 'g0' and 'sigma' is specific to the particular shape of detection function that is fitted (e.g. halfnormal or negative exponential). In other words, we don't expect sigma-hat from the half normal to be the same as sigma-hat from the negative exponential - they relate to different parameters. This is certainly a potential trap. (One can compare the area of a circle enclosing, say, 95% of an equivalent 2-D activity distribution = home-range model, but that is getting rather technical and it is probably better done using lambda0 in the cumulative hazard parameterization (HHN, HEX). I'm not suggesting you do that, just indicating the possibility).
Murray

messages.subject_clean: calculate or extract SE of Density from fitted SECR model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Eric,

The link-scale SE is not typically meaningful on the real scale.  You can back-transform the confidence intervals of course, but in doing so you should notice that they are not symmetrical.  Technically it is possible to approximate an SE on the real scale, but most folks do not bother.

messages.subject: Re: calculate or extract SE of Density from fitted SECR model
messages.subject_clean: calculate or extract SE of Density from fitted SECR model
messages.body_plain:
I don't know about 'most folks', but the delta method SE (for which I presume Eric found the reference in the help) does have its uses as a single-value summary of precision, and as the basis for RSE(D-hat) (or CV(D-hat) as some like to call it). Of course it is a mistake to use +/- 2SE on the 'real' scale as a CI.
Murray

messages.subject: Spatially explicit capture-recapture course July 5-7
messages.body_plain:
The Columbia Mountains Institute is offering a 3-day course on spatially explicit capture–recapture (SECR) at Selkirk College, Castlegar, British Columbia, on 5–7 July 2016 (instructor Murray Efford).

The aim of this course is to give participants a practical understanding of SECR and its limitations through the experience of fitting models with the R package ‘secr’. Topics to be covered include:

-       concepts and assumptions underlying SECR

-       data preparation and checking

-       model fitting and evaluation

-       study design

Advanced topics will be included as requested.

The course fee is CND$575. Reasonably priced accommodation is available on campus.

See the CMI website for further information: http://cmiae.org/event/spatially-explicit-capture-recapture-secr-modeling/

or contact Murray Efford directly.

messages.subject_clean: Problems loading capture history in boundary polygon
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,
I am trying to view my capture history data (of rats) in my boundary polygon but got some warning and error messages. I can't seem to find where the problem is coming from.
I will gladly appreciate some help.  Attached is some part of my capture history, and trap data plus the shapefile I used for my boundary polygon.
Biplang

library(maptools)
library(RMark)
library(maptools)
library(rgeos)
library(secr)
ratpol <- readShapePoly("nn4secr1")
plot(ratpol)
ratCH<- read.capthist('RealCapt1.2.txt', 'Critrap2.2.txt',detector = 'proximity')
summary(ratCH)

#I got warning that some traps are not in the habitat polygon
ratmask<- make.mask(traps(ratCH), spacing = 40,
                         buffer = 150, type = "trapbuffer", poly =ratpol)
"Warning messages:
1: In make.mask(traps(ratCH), spacing = 40, buffer = 150, type = "trapbuffer",  :
  some traps are not inside habitat polygon
2: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
3: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
4: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
5: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf"
par(mar = c(1,6,6,6), xpd = TRUE)
plot (ratmask, ppoly = TRUE) # I get an error output
"Error in if (yuin > xuin * ratio) yuin <- xuin * ratio else xuin <- yuin/ratio :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
2: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
3: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
4: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf"
#The capture events did not show on my boundary polygon
plot(ratpol)
plot(ratCH,add=TRUE)
#But the traps all apear in the boundary polygon
plot(ratpol)
plot(traps(ratCH),add=TRUE)

#N.B. shape file and trap text file are in "decimal degrees"
 #and CRS(EPSG:4326, WGS 84)

messages.subject: Re: Problems loading capture history in boundary polygon
messages.subject_clean: Problems loading capture history in boundary polygon
messages.body_plain:
Hello Yadok
You are asking for trouble by using decimal degrees as your units (even near the equator). The default units in 'secr' are metres. Your code works if you make all the conversions (I'm guessing one degree is roughly 110000 metres square), e.g.

ratmask<- make.mask(traps(ratCH), spacing = 40/110000,
                    buffer = 150/110000, type = "trapbuffer", poly =ratpol)

And remember that the default border for plots in 'secr' is 100 metres and the default 'rad' argument is 5 metres.

I think the smart thing might be to project your polygon to metric coordinates (UTM?) using spTransform in rgdal, and also your trap coordinates. That may take some time for you to figure out, but it's a useful skill!
Murray
